notes.title: 0.4.0 - The Ride of the Valkyrie
notes.content: [p]Alpha Demo 0.4.0 is now available to download and play - adding the second playable aircraft, and two new missions for you and your wingmen to fly it in![/p][h1]What's new?[/h1][h2]The Valkyrie[/h2][p]The counterpart of the fast, agile Phoenix, the second playable aircraft is a heavily armed and armored juggernaut purpose-built for ground-attack missions. Pilot the Valkyrie yourself to take advantage of its higher resilience and much stronger main gun, or assign them to your wingmen so they can destroy ground targets even faster.[/p][p]The Valkyrie's unique R&D stat is [b]Firepower[/b], increasing both reload speed and maximum ammo capacity - allowing you to wreak even more havoc on enemy ground targets.[/p][h3]Primary Weapons[/h3][list][*][p][b]Seeker Missiles[/b] - a pair of reliable homing missiles, as on the Phoenix.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Auxiliary Guns[/b] - four more rotary cannon, for when your main gun just isn't enough.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Burst Lasers[/b] - high-power, short-duration laser cannon, as on the Phoenix.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Plasma Throwers[/b] - continuously spray superheated plasma in a cone in front of you, suitable for melting planes and tanks alike.[/p][/*][/list][h3]Secondary Weapons[/h3][list][*][p][b]Hydra Missiles[/b] - cruise missiles that split into smaller guided missiles just before they reach their target, hitting other high-value targets nearby. Their high range makes them handy for eliminating a base's defenses from outside retaliation range.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Quake Rockets[/b] - automatic volley-fire of up to 10 unguided, high-explosive rockets at a time, great for saturation bombardments.[/p][/*][*][p][b]Splitter Cannon[/b] - gigantic double-barrelled cannon that fire hundreds of submunitions with a wide spread. The recoil is enough to knock your plane backwards, so be careful you don't stall![/p][/*][/list][p][/p][h2]New Missions[/h2][p]The two new missions in 0.4.0 take place around one of Jupiter's massive floating [b]cityships[/b], a turbine-powered platform with both its upper and lower surfaces covered in skyscrapers.[/p][p]The [b]Urban Defence[/b] mission requires you to protect a cityship from the CLE's three-pronged assault, as they aim to knock it out of the sky by destroying its turbines. You'll have to help allied forces keep the six giant turbines safe by intercepting the enemy before they can reach them![/p][p]Meanwhile, the [b]Urban Assault[/b] mission sees the INDF taking the fight onto the surface of the cityship itself in a chaotic ground battle between allied and enemy forces. You'll need to weave between the skyscrapers and destroy the ground units in their shadows in order to win - whether it's through strafing runs in Flight Mode, or pinpoint bombardments from Hover Mode.[/p][p][/p][h2]Mission Layout Improvements[/h2][p]New tech built for the urban warfare missions has been carried over to the rest of the game, refining the way units and structures are spawned. You'll find that both allies and enemies spawn in [b]more concentrated clusters[/b], leaving the map less cluttered and making it easier to pick your next group of targets.[/p][p][/p][h2]New Ground Units[/h2][p]Both sides of the conflict have deployed some brand-new units to the Urban Assault and Urban Defense missions:[/p][p]INDF allies make landfall for the first time with their agile, floating ground units - sturdy [b]hover tanks[/b] with resilient shields and anti-armor cannon, backed up by [b]self-propelled AA units[/b] providing defense against enemy planes, and [b]tank destroyers[/b] that can use their railguns to snipe enemies from a distance. With careful choice of targets and close air support, you can keep these units alive in missions, allowing them to back you up and earn you even more points![/p][p]On the other end of the battlefield, enemy tanks have been reinforced by [b]quadmechs[/b], large quadrupedal robots that can [b]cling to walls and ceilings[/b] to reach better vantage points. Anti-armor quadmechs tower over other ground units and have devastating firepower, but the key enemies to watch out for are the [b]AA quadmech variants[/b] that can climb onto rooftops to fire both autocannon and missiles at you![/p][p] [/p][h2]Visual Improvements[/h2][p]As the beginning of a game-wide visual overhaul, every shielded vehicle in the game has been revamped to use new [b]shield bubbles[/b] that are more visually recognisable from a distance, show a visual cue when the unit's shield starts recharging, and has better performance to boot![/p][p]All aircraft have also received replacement [b]thruster exhaust VFX[/b], including enemy planes like Goblins and Manticores that previously didn't have any - look out for the glowing flares behind them in night-time missions![/p][p][/p][h2]Minor Improvements[/h2][list][*][p]Updated briefing screen UI[/p][/*][*][p]Briefing dialogue text now wraps correctly[/p][/*][*][p]Briefing dialogue can now be skipped through[/p][/*][*][p]The default controller mapping for Target Cam is now the right stick[/p][/*][*][p]While Target Cam is active, use the right stick to switch targets[/p][/*][*][p]Renamed the "Default" flight system to "Precision"[/p][/*][*][p]Button mappings are now displayed on menu tabs[/p][/*][/list][h2]Bugfixes[/h2][list][*][p]Prevented plane colour schemes from becoming corrupted under certain circumstances[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed an issue causing wingmen to lose their invulnerability[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed unusual movement behavior when navigating menus[/p][/*][*][p]Available missions now update correctly when aborting runs[/p][/*][*][p]Mission select button backgrounds now resize correctly[/p][/*][*][p]Prevented unintentional inputs when switching between Hover and Flight mode[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed erroneous mapping icons in the Tutorial[/p][/*][*][p]Fixed issues with Prototype Upgrade behavior[/p][/*][/list][h1]So what's next?[/h1][p]0.4.0 finishes setting up most of the systems needed to make Nova Squadron a solid gameplay proof-of-concept - mission generation, aircraft choices and upgrades, ground combat, and so on. From here on, then, it's time to move away from the core gameplay loop and start making Nova Squadron more of a fully-fledged, detailed game in 0.5.0:[/p][list][*][p]Better progression between missions[/p][/*][*][p]More sophisticated options and decision-making[/p][/*][*][p]Embedded lore and narrative[/p][/*][*][p]Characters you can [b]talk to and build relationships with[/b]![/p][/*][/list][p]For now though, we hope you enjoy flying the Valkyrie, experimenting with its weapons, and weaving between skyscrapers in Alpha Demo 0.4.0![/p]

notes.title: 0.3.0 - The Reinforcements Update
notes.content:
Alpha Demo 0.3.0, the Reinforcements Update, is now available to download and play! This update brings with it a full balance rework of the entire game, and new tools at both you and your enemies' disposal.
[b]Due to the extensive changes to the game's internal systems, your current run will be reset when booting 0.3.0. All other progression in your save file is unaffected.[/b]

[h1]What's new?[/h1]
[h2]Reinforcement Waves[/h2]
At regular time intervals, or under certain conditions, [b]new waves of allies and/or enemies will spawn mid-mission[/b]! You'll find that missions in 0.3.0 stay packed with enemies to fight, and if you're not careful missions can snowball out of control as more and more enemies attack you at once.

[h2]Fire Support[/h2]
As you earn points by destroying targets, you'll fill up a Fire Support gauge. Once this is full, you can press a button to [b]request a strike on your current target[/b] and up to 9 nearby enemies! Any allied units can respond to these requests, from your wingmen to airships - but if you call in Fire Support on a ground target, you might see the INDF's [b]orbital railgun satellite network[/b] respond to the request!
[i]For existing players: the Fire Support button is an additional control binding. If you've customised your bindings, you may need to manually add this extra binding before being able to use Fire Support.[/i]

[h2]New Units[/h2]
[h3]Bomber Rework[/h3]
The Manticore bomber has had a full remodel, and is now able to fight back with its tail-mounted autocannon! On higher difficulties, you might also see the up-armoured and up-gunned Chimera, which carries a [b]high-powered defense laser[/b].

[h3]The Strigoi and Vampire[/h3]
Joining the Kobold light fighter is the Strigoi multirole and its modernised variant, the Vampire! These come in two forms, the Type/F (Fighter loadout, with anti-air missiles) and the Type/A (Attacker loadout, with anti-ship rocket pods).

[h3]Allied Frigates[/h3]
The INDF's laser destroyers are now joined by smaller, lighter frigates equipped with missile launchers. You can find these in the Naval Escort and Naval Battle missions, where they'll support the destroyers by defending against Strigoi/A raids.

[h2]Prototype Upgrades[/h2]
You can now find and purchase Prototype Upgrades in the Upgrades menu! These are a range of [b]extremely powerful upgrades[/b] that provide an advantage in combat, but come with [b]dangerous drawbacks[/b] that you'll need to adjust your fighting style to handle. For example, there are Prototype Upgrades that replace your machine gun or secondary weapon entirely, or reduce your max health to make every one of your attacks explosive!

[h2]Township Revamp[/h2]
The huge floating metal doughnuts in the sky have been re-engineered and given a fresh coat of paint! Destroy the infrastructure built on top of them, or break open their bulkhead doors and [b]fly inside[/b] to take out the Callistan fleet in the dry docks.

[h2]Naval Escort Mission[/h2]
You can now sortie into the new Naval Escort mission type, where instead of destroying targets, your job is to keep as many of your own units alive as possible! A column of allied frigates and destroyers will come under attack by waves of Strigoi and Vampires, and you'll need to intercept them before they can wreak havoc on the allied fleet.

[h2]Minor Improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*] HUD kill feed now shows all recently destroyed enemies, instead of just the latest one
[*] The HUD target counter no longer replaces the score counter, and has a label for whether targets should be protected or destroyed
[*] Difficulty levels have been renamed
[*] All missions have been rebalanced to account for the new mechanics
[*] New BGM for the ICBM mission update, replacing the regular mission music
[*] New BGM variant for the Mission 4 briefing
[*] Maps are now different sizes and shapes for different missions
[*] Swapped the MG and shield cooldown sound effects
[*] Added a "magazine empty" click when attempting to fire weapons that are still reloading
[*] Wingmen will now return if they end up too far away from you
[*] Enemy aircraft will move faster when chasing targets
[*] Added upgrade dialogs on boot that explain some of the new changes
[/list]

[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*] Fixed an issue causing ICBMs to explode instantly when hit
[*] Fixed a crash during the tutorial mission
[*] Fixed the incorrect Sell mapping glyph in the Parts menu
[/list]

[h1]So what's next?[/h1]
0.3.0 largely finishes the overhauls to the game's internal systems and code, leaving it in a stable state to be expanded upon and added to. And 0.4.0 will do just that with a couple of massive features:
[list]
[*] The second playable aircraft, the Valkyrie
[*] New weapons that add extra gameplay options
[*] Two new missions on a larger scale than anything in the game so far
[/list]
We hope you enjoy playing Alpha Demo 0.3.0 and experimenting with the new Prototype Upgrades!

notes.title: Nova Squadron Alpha Demo 0.2.0 - The KBM Update
notes.content:
Alpha Demo 0.2.0, the Keyboard and Mouse Update, is now available to download and play! [b]This update brings with it multiple stability improvements to help prevent the game from freezing or becoming unresponsive.[/b]

[h1]What's new?[/h1]
[h2]Improved keyboard and mouse support[/h2]
[list]
[*]Keyboard-only control schemes are now supported, and have their own default scheme
[*]Every control in the game is now fully rebindable on keyboard and mouse
[*]Boost Turning and switching to/from hover mode now have their own individual keybindings
[*]UI glyphs now update to indicate your current control scheme
[/list]
[h2]Stat system overhaul[/h2]
[list]
[*]The Phoenix's base pitch, roll and yaw mobility has been substantially increased
[*]Defense and Cannon R&D stats have been removed and replaced
[*]New R&D stat: Targeting - increases the range and lock-on speed of all weapons
[*]New R&D stat: Resilience - increases hull and shield strength; decreases damage taken while ramming
[*]New R&D stat: Boost - increases maximum Boost Turn charge, allowing you to Boost Turn for longer
[*][i]For existing players:[/i] points previously invested into Defense and Cannon can be redistributed to other stats and are not lost
[/list]
[h2]Better first-time boot flow[/h2]
[list]
[*]Flight system and audio settings are now directly shown on first boot
[*]The tutorial can now be skipped, and is accessible at any time from the mission select screen
[*]The tutorial's instructions are now clearer and will update when switching between controller and KBM
[*]You can get straight into the action on first boot without having to go through the settings menu first
[*][i]For existing players:[/i] the new first-time boot flow will be shown the next time you boot up the game
[/list]
[h2]New HUD elements[/h2]
[list]
[*]A new combo counter indicates how many missiles you've hit with and targets you've destroyed within a few seconds of each other
[*]Objective alerts will now appear whenever you complete an objective or are given a new one
[/list]
[h2]General improvements[/h2]
[list]
[*]Pitch/roll and yaw sensitivity can now be adjusted
[*]The mapping glyphs at the bottom of menus now update in real time to show your current control scheme
[*]Added specific mapping glyphs for various controllers
[*]Improved frame rate in certain menus
[*]Reworked the background music on the main menu
[*]Added unique background music for nighttime missions
[/list]
[h2]Bugfixes[/h2]
[list]
[*][b]Fixed issues that were causing the game to freeze on boot for some players[/b]
[*][b]Fixed issues preventing some players from using either their controller or keyboard[/b]
[*]Prevented tutorial targets from spawning inside the cloud layer
[*]Stopped the HUD cooling gauge from breaking when a large number of machine gun cooldown upgrades are purchased
[*]Fixed issues affecting ram damage dealt and taken - ramming is now more reliable and on average deals more damage
[*]Corrected misleading mapping glyphs on some menus
[*]Fixed the speed at which the intro text advances in the tutorial on lower frame rates
[*]...and various other minor fixes throughout the game
[/list]
[h1]So what's next?[/h1]
Since the 0.1.0 release, there have been multiple unexpected roadblocks with development, and these have caused this first update to take a lot longer than we were expecting. Fixing some of the freezes and crashes players reported, as well as the improved input system and keyboard support, led to a full overhaul of most of the game's underlying systems - the code is in a much better state now, so this isn't something we should need to do twice.

Now that 0.2.0 is out, development of new gameplay systems, missions, enemies, and playable aircraft will finally be moving forward! In 0.3.0, you can expect to see:
[list]
[*]More tightly packed missions, with more enemies and targets to destroy
[*]New enemy types to [strike]get blown up by[/strike] take down
[*]Tougher missions and more deadly opponents
[*]More involvement of the allied navy in missions
[*]New mission types and objectives
[/list]
We hope you enjoy playing Alpha Demo 0.2.0, and can't wait for you to see what's coming up next in 0.3.0!

notes.title: Nova Squadron Alpha Demo 0.1.0 is out now!
notes.content:
The Nova Squadron alpha demo is now available to play on Windows and Linux via Proton!

[h2]So what's in the demo?[/h2]
You'll have access to the first four procedural missions of the roguelite campaign, and use Credits to upgrade your plane mid-campaign - whether you win or lose, you'll keep all the Renown you earned in that campaign and be able to buy permanent upgrades afterwards, then go into another campaign attempt on the same or a different difficulty. There's no time limit, so feel free to hunt down every part and buy every Research Point!

[h2]How's the controller support?[/h2]
0.1.0 has full controller support via Steam Input, so it should support anything that Steam itself recognises. You can also remap and customise your control scheme via the interface in the Steam client.
Unfortunately, some other features have been temporarily disabled for this version; keyboard and mouse is fully supported but you won't be able to remap the default control scheme currently. Flight stick support is on its way.
At the moment it's strongly recommended that you play Nova Squadron with a controller.

[h2]What happens next?[/h2]
The Nova Squadron demo will be receiving regular updates over the coming months, including:
[list]
[*]The Valkyrie, a new ground-attack plane to equip your squadron with
[*]Cockpit (first-person) view
[*]New enemies, such as the Serpent fighter plane and Chimera heavy bomber
[*]New mission types
[*]Improved hangar visuals and flow
[*]macOS support
[/list]
[i]These features, and the order in which they are added, may change.[/i]

We hope you enjoy the 0.1.0 alpha demo, and look forward to seeing you defeat Sceptre Squadron!
